headline: Petition to extend a sidewalk on Ararat Street to Indian Hill Road, and a proposed review of the street and sidewalk resurfacing process.
summary: Adela Melendez asks that the existing Ararat St. sidewalk be extended to include 139 Ararat St., up to its intersection with Indian Hill Rd. Councilor Tony Economou asks the City Manager to review rules so that streets and sidewalks go directly to the appropriate department for review under the Pavement Management Program.
items: Petition to extend the Ararat St. sidewalk to 139 Ararat St. and Indian Hill Rd.
Order to review the street and sidewalk resurfacing process
location: Esther Howland (South) Chamber, City Hall, 455 Main Street, Worcester, Massachusetts

. Virtual Attendee Call-In Information/Important Notice to Residents 1 
Pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 2021 and in order to ensure active, public 
engagement, the City of Worcester currently allows for both in -person and remote 
participation at all City Council and Standing Committee meetings. To partake in the 
meeting, you may attend the meeting in -person within the meeting location, follow the 
below link to join via Zoom or dial the direct line as indicated. If you join a Zoom 
meeting by dialing in with a phone number, you can raise your hand by dialing *9.

a.
Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the impersonation 
of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting payments be 
made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions. All official 
emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an @worcesterma.gov email 
address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail on the City of 
Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always include your 
specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, and location . 
The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.

. Miscellaneous Item 4 
Order of Councilor Tony Economou - Request City Manager request City Solicitor work 
with the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and Commissioner of Public 
Works to review the city’s ordinances and /or regulations associated with street and 
sidewalk resurfacing program to amend the process to become a more administrative 
function wherein the streets and sidewalks are submitted directly to the appropriate 
department for immediate review and consideration as part of the city’s Pavement 
Management Program. Said review should maintain City Council oversight by including 
the streets and sidewalks added to the resurfacing lists as part of the city’s monthly 
Construction Progress Reports.
